thread.title: The presidency doesn’t require a mental health evaluation, but these jobs do...

author: Maria LaMagna
title: The presidency doesn’t require a mental health evaluation, but these jobs do...
text:
Carl Bernstein, renowned for his reporting on the Watergate scandal, on Sunday questioned President Trump’s ability to govern .
“We’re in a real constitutional crisis ...in which a huge part of the citizenry of our country and the leadership of the country in Congress, privately and in public, openly question the fitness and stability of the president of the United States,” Bernstein told CNN, where he is now a contributor. 
Commercial pilots are required to meet medical standards including blood pressure, hearing and vision requirements and be free from certain mental illnesses. Bernstein’s comments came after the release of the book “Fire and Fury: Inside the Trump White House” by Michael Wolff. The book, which Trump has said is “full of lies,” raises questions about Trump’s mental health. In response, the president tweeted that he is a “stable genius.” 
When it comes to a president’s mental health, the stakes are obviously high, especially when he tweets about the size of his nuclear button . But a world leader isn’t the only one who has to navigate these types of questions.
Nearly one in five Americans say they’ve experienced mental illness at some point in their lives , according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. Millions of people with mental illnesses are able to successfully do their jobs, although it is estimated that only about 70% of people who experience serious mental illnesses receive treatment in a given year. 
Here’s what employers are and are not allowed to ask. 
1. Jobs where mental health can be an issue 
Some jobs require additional licenses or certifications that require further medical testing — particularly jobs in public service or transportation, which could put others’ lives at risk, said Chris Kuczynski, the acting associate legal counsel at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. That applies to mental and physical health.
• Commercial pilots are required to meet medical standards including blood pressure, hearing and vision and be free from certain mental illnesses, including psychosis, bipolar disorder or severe personality disorders. 
• The Federal Aviation Administration also has a series of rules that governs the self-reporting of pilots who take antidepressants. 
• Many states ask about mental-illness diagnosis and treatment when issuing medical licenses , according to the Journal of Medical Licensing and Discipline. 
Thirteen of those states told the Journal of Medical Licensing and Discipline that any report of mental illness is sufficient for imposing consequences, including revoking or restricting a license. 
• Some states have asked similar questions of lawyers when distributing their licenses and some legal experts say seeking treatment for mental health conditions is a good thing.
• It’s common for corporate executives to have provisions written into their contracts about what would happen if their age or health made them unable to do their jobs.
• New York City taxi drivers must have a medical exam within 90 days of applying for a license , and submit their results to the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission. 
Some states ask about mental-illness diagnosis and treatment when issuing medical licenses. Over a dozen say that a report of mental illness is sufficient for imposing consequences, including revoking or restricting a license. Prospective NYC taxi drivers must take a drug test, and the evaluation form also alludes to mental health: “Medically fit means that the applicant is of sound physical condition with good eyesight and no epilepsy, vertigo, heart trouble or any other infirmity of body or mind to the extent that it would render the applicant unfit for the safe operation of a licensed vehicle at all times of the day.”
Many states have “ pre-employment psychological evaluations ” for law enforcement candidates. Law enforcement officers and firefighters also have their own set of health and physical fitness standards they must meet. And drivers of commercial motor vehicles, such as trucks, have to maintain a current medical examiner’s certificate in order to drive.
However, the law protects executives from how much information shareholders are able to seek about executives’ medical conditions; all questions would have to be directly related to the job and consistent with “business necessity,” Rsaid Merrick Rossein, a professor at City University of New York Law School. 
If there’s objective evidence that an executive is having issues affecting his or her judgement, it may be legal for shareholders or other members of the corporation to ask him or her to have a medical exam, Rossein said.
New York City taxi drivers must have a medical exam within 90 days of applying for a license, and submit the results to the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission. The evaluation form also alludes to mental health. “If the CEO is falling asleep at a press conference, or started slurring his or her words, I think they could require him or her to have a medical examination,” he said.
The amount of information CEOs should disclose about their health has been debated in the past. Steve Jobs, the late chief executive of Apple AAPL, -0.37% , was criticized for not publicly disclosing more information about his health after he was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. Jobs sent an email to Apple employees in 2004 telling them he had a cancerous tumor removed from his pancreas, but questions about his health rose again in 2008 when he appeared to be thin and sick at public events. 
2. Most of the time, prospective employers can’t ask about your mental health 
There are several laws that protect job candidates from employers’ questions about their health, including their mental health.
The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), determines what information employers are allowed to ask prospective employees about their health , with the goal of protecting those who could perform their jobs with some accommodations for their disabilities. Employers aren’t allowed to ask job applicants to take any medical exams, nor ask applicants about any disabilities they may or may not have, before extending a job offer. 
The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 puts restrictions on who is allowed to see medical information; health information generally can’t be used for purposes not directly related to care without an individual’s permission. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) also puts restrictions on who is allowed to see medical information; health information generally can’t be used for purposes not directly related to care without an individual’s permission. Under HIPAA, a doctor, for example, can’t give health information to an employer without the employee or applicant’s permission. 
Employees are also protected from discrimination simply because they have mental health conditions, according to the EEOC. In fact, employees are entitled to “reasonable accommodations” for mental health conditions that can help them keep and perform their jobs.
